title: Gnome World’s Speed Run, Frame by Frame
blurb: Why Gnome world's speed run played at a poor frame rate, with frames of hundreds of milliseconds on a busy laptop, and what 0.0.149 changes. Not Hazel: its compiled rules are 1.3% to 1.8% of the page's busy time, and with every piece in plain JavaScript the frames are the same. The run gave its steps a fixed 12 ms of every frame, so any drawing over 4.7 ms missed the screen's refresh; and each picture coming into view was painted in the frame that showed it, several at once. Now the steps take what the frame leaves, and a frame paints 4 ms of new pictures: in a 1920×1080 window at 2×, 30 fps becomes 60 fps. Hazel is 10% of the code.
